To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

action potential firing of myelinated hippocampal CA1 axons results in the production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen radicals that diffuse to nearby oligodendroglia and cause post-translational modification of the oligodendoncyte-specific protein MBP.

action potential activity in myelinated axons results in the generation of reactive oxygen species, which are released from the axons and act as signaling molecules to activate oligodendroglial cells, which in turn regulate the phosphorylation status of myelin basic protein, a major structural protein of myelin.
action potentials in CA1 pyramidal cell axons increase the phosphorylation of myelin basic protein in oligodendroglia, and this effect is mediated by reactive oxygen and nitrogen intermediates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of reactive oxygen and reactive nitrogen species in the modulation of neuronal function.
the study of the mechanisms of action of the neuroactive steroids and their role in the regulation of neuronal activity.
the role that glia play in activity-dependent changes in neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
reactive oxygen species mediate activity-dependent neuron–oligodendrocytic signaling in output fibers of the hippocampus.

the results indicate that, under conditions of increased neuronal activity, reactive oxygen and reactive nitrogen species are generated in hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons and diffuse to neighboring oligdendrocytes, where they activate signaling cascades leading to post-translational modification of MBP.

the results of the present study indicate that, in the output fibers of the hippocampus (the alveus), the generation of reactive oxygen and reactive nitrogen species by action potentials results in a post-translational modification of the myelin-specific protein MBP in the oligodendocyte cell membrane, which is the first step in a neuron–oligodendocyte signaling pathway.

the hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons can signal to the oligodendocytes through reactive oxygen and nitrogen.
the reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated in the hippocampus during high-frequency neuronal firing are involved in the regulation of oligodendroglia and myelin in the hippocampus.

The main takeaway from our work is that
neurons can communicate with glia in the absence of synaptic signaling.
reactive oxygen species are important mediators of activity-dependent signaling in the nervous system, and this is not limited to the synapse.
neurons can communicate with their glial neighbors in a nonsynaptic, activity-dependent manner.
